_readme: PRIMARY ENGLISH BY GRADE - GRADES 3, 4 AND 5
There are deliberately NO Grade 1 or Grade 2 pages. The Drive holds no
Grade 1 or Grade 2 syllabus, Pupil's Book or Teacher's Guide, so there
is nothing to build a page from. Both grades stay VISIBLE on the
Primary English hub as non-clickable cards marked 'Resources in
preparation'. Do not create pages for them until real material exists.
Every statement on the three pages below is taken from the NIE English
Language Teachers' Guide for THAT grade. Nothing is carried across from
one grade to another, and nothing is generic.
Grade 3 - Teachers' Guide Grade 03, first edition 2017, from 2018
Grade 5 - Teachers' Guide Grade 05, first edition 2020
Primary English uses FOUR competencies organised by skill:
This is a third framework, separate from Grade 6 (2026) and from
Grades 7-11. Never carry a primary competency number upward.

is linked from Grade 5, never merged into ordinary syllabus work.

pages.title: Grade 3 English
pages.metaTitle: Grade 3 English | Primary English | RCF English
pages.description: Grade 3 English following the NIE primary syllabus: alphabet sounds, words of three or four letters, sentences of up to five words, capital letters and full stops.
pages.keywords: Grade 3 English Sri Lanka, primary English grade 3, alphabet sounds, this that, capital letters

hero.text: Grade 3 English: the year the letters become words, and the words become short sentences.

blocks.heading: What Grade 3 covers
text: Grade 3 works in four skill competencies — **listening, speaking, reading and writing**. Alphabet work, vocabulary, language patterns, poems and games are not separate subjects; they sit inside those four.
The year is built on very short units of language. Words of **three or four letters**, lists of **five to ten known words**, and reading sentences that do **not exceed five words**.

blocks.heading: The four competencies in Grade 3
columns: What the syllabus asks for at this grade
rows: Listening
Identifying the sound each letter of the alphabet makes, and matching letters to sounds aloud.
Speaking
Verbally matching the letters of the alphabet; naming nouns and verbs from the child's immediate surroundings.
Reading
Reading a list of five to ten known words. Reading and understanding **this** and **that** in context. Simple texts with sentences of no more than five words.
Writing
Writing the letters of the alphabet independently. Beginning a sentence with a capital letter, writing a name with a capital first letter, and ending with a full stop.

blocks.heading: Vocabulary and language patterns
text: Grade 3 introduces **article–noun** and **adjective–noun** combinations, and the verbs that go with everyday surroundings. Numbers are used up to a total of **twenty**, with the ordinals **1st, 2nd, 3rd** and *the last*. Shapes in the immediate environment are named and described.
Source: *English Language Teachers' Guide, Grade 03*, Department of English, National Institute of Education, Maharagama, first edition 2017, to be implemented from 2018.

items.title: Alphabet and phonics
text: Letter names against letter sounds, and blending sounds into words — the Grade 3 starting point.

items.title: Poems and rhymes
text: Rhyme makes the sounds of English easier to hear, which is what listening asks for here.

items.title: Games and practice
text: Letter, word and sentence activities that mark themselves.

blocks.title: Still being prepared for Grade 3
text: Graded word lists of five to ten words, **this/that** practice, and writing exercises for capital letters and full stops are being prepared against the Grade 3 Teacher's Guide. They will appear here as each is checked.

pages.title: Grade 4 English
pages.metaTitle: Grade 4 English | Primary English | RCF English
pages.description: Grade 4 English following the NIE primary syllabus: short and long vowel sounds, personal and possessive pronouns, numbers to 50, and writing with correct punctuation.
pages.keywords: Grade 4 English Sri Lanka, primary English grade 4, pronouns, vowel sounds, ordinals

hero.text: Grade 4 English: longer sentences, pronouns used accurately, and writing that is properly punctuated.

blocks.heading: What Grade 4 covers
text: The same four competencies continue — **listening, speaking, reading and writing** — but the language widens. Grade 4 is where pronouns, polite requests and larger numbers are expected to be used correctly rather than merely recognised.

blocks.heading: The four competencies in Grade 4
columns: What the syllabus asks for at this grade
rows: Listening

Understanding questions about personal information, likes and dislikes, abilities, polite offers and requests, and simple instructions and directions. Recognising cardinal numbers 0–50 and ordinals to 31st.
Speaking

Pronouncing short and long vowel sounds correctly. Using personal, possessive and object pronouns. Introducing others, describing animals and places, expressing feelings, asking and answering about likes and abilities.
Reading
Reading aloud words with short and long vowel sounds. Extracting specific information — names, things, places, numbers — from texts of five to eight sentences.
Writing
Copying words with correct letter formation, size and spacing. Using the **period and the question mark** appropriately. Writing simple sentences with correct spacing between words.

blocks.heading: Vocabulary and language patterns
text: Grade 4 works with **SV, SVO and SVC sentence patterns** through controlled writing, and with nouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs in sentences. Shapes, distances and measurements are named, and there is a defined strand of **science and technology vocabulary** — operating a computer, tablet or telephone, and talking about plants, animals and insects in the immediate environment.
Source: *English Language Teachers' Guide, Grade 04*, Department of English, National Institute of Education, Maharagama.

items.title: Reading
text: Short passages with questions — the five-to-eight sentence length Grade 4 expects.

items.title: Listening and speaking

items.title: Games and practice

hero.text: Grade 5 English: three tenses, the texts of everyday life, and writing that is accurate on its own.

blocks.heading: What Grade 5 covers
text: Grade 5 draws the primary years together. The four competencies are unchanged, but the texts become the ones children meet outside the classroom, and writing is expected to be accurate without help.

blocks.heading: The four competencies in Grade 5
columns: What the syllabus asks for at this grade
rows: Listening
Responding to questions on familiar topics, both information and confirmation questions, using **Who, When, What** and **Where**. Following announcements, dialogues, verbal messages and instructions.
Speaking
Pronouncing words, phrases and sentences properly, including the vowel rules — silent **e** as in *cake*, and two vowel letters making one sound. Using personal pronouns in sentences.
Reading
Reading the texts of daily life: **notices, leaflets, train and bus timetables, brochures, restaurant menus, advertisements and recipes**, as well as posters and labels.
Writing
Writing simple sentences on a given topic accurately, with correct **spelling, spacing between words and punctuation**. Copying addresses, lists of names and shopping lists.

blocks.heading: Tenses and text types
text: Grade 5 texts use three tenses: **simple present, simple past and present continuous**. The text types named are simple descriptions, informative texts, short stories, announcements, invitations, poems and dialogues.
Source: *English Language Teachers' Guide, Grade 05*, Department of English, National Institute of Education, Maharagama, first edition 2020.

blocks.title: Scholarship English is a separate thing
text: The Grade 5 Scholarship examination is not the ordinary Grade 5 English syllabus, and the two are never mixed here. The scholarship work has its own page: [Grade 5 Scholarship](primary-english/grade-5-scholarship/).
